Modified assessment: The Committee adopts a cautiously dovish stance. While labor markets and household spending remain strong, the statement highlights persistent weakness in business fixed investment and exports and inflation running below the 2 percent objective with low market-based inflation compensation. Consistent with the literature that investment shortfalls often account for downturns in real GDP and amplify business cycles, the weakness in business fixed investment weighs on the outlook. The emphasis on muted inflation pressures aligns with models where expected inflation shapes current inflation dynamics (e.g., Cagan-type expectations and New Keynesian Phillips curve evidence from Galí, Gertler, and López-Salido), justifying accommodation to prevent expectations from drifting lower. The rate cut to 1.50–1.75 percent, the lower interest on reserves (1.55 percent), and T-bill purchases plus repo operations to maintain ample reserves are consistent with evidence that monetary policy affects real activity in the short run (McCallum and Nelson; B. Friedman) and that exogenous policy shocks transmit to real output (Sims). Net tone: constructive on current activity but clearly risk-aware and easing-biased due to weak investment and below-target inflation.
